## Mose 0.1.43
**New** - This Mac has its own page under Devices: a drawing of the Mac with each port and what's plugged into it, the charger, the battery and the displays. Click a port, the battery or a display for the details. - Cables: every cable with a chip is remembered. Name it and pick its colour, and see what it can carry (power, data, video), who made it, how often and how long it's been used, and whether it has dropped out or hit overcurrent. Cables without a chip show while they're plugged in. - Charging in plain words: running on the charger with the battery held near full, a cable rated below the charger, or slowing as the battery fills. A curve shows the power from the charger and what the Mac used over the last hour. - A notification when a plugged-in cable drops out or hits overcurrent. Turn it off in Settings › Battery. - Displays: whether each one runs at its best, and what holds it back (a hub keeping lanes for USB, a slow cable, or a setting). Change a display's size from the Mac page. A USB-C monitor that also charges the Mac shows both. - Hubs and docks: devices are listed by what they're plugged into, and Thunderbolt docks by name. - How each mouse, keyboard and receiver reaches the Mac, from its page: receiver, hub and port. Mose warns when a receiver shares a hub with a USB 3 device, which can disturb 2.4 GHz. - The menu bar shows this Mac and its ports.
**Fixed** - Keyboards with mouse keys (many QMK keyboards, such as the NuPhy Kick75) show up as keyboards, not mice.
Requires macOS 15 or later. Ports, cables and displays need a Mac with Apple silicon.

## Mose 0.1.42
**Fixed** - Mose no longer quits unexpectedly every so often while trackpad gestures are turned on.
Requires macOS 15 or later.

## Mose 0.1.41
**New** - Keyboards in the sidebar. Each keyboard gets a page that draws it with your layout and lights up the keys as you press them. - Remap keys: any key, with or without fn, everywhere or only in one app. Caps Lock and the modifier keys can be remapped too (Caps Lock → Escape, for example). macOS itself does those, so they work in password fields as well. - Logitech keyboards: battery, backlight, the top row as media keys or F1–F12, Easy-Switch channels, and remappable special keys. - Keystroke stats for each keyboard, by hour and by key, on its page and in Usage Stats. Only counts are kept, never what you type. Turn it off in Settings › Usage Stats. - Trackpad holds: rest three or four fingers, or one finger in a top corner, and the action stays held until you lift. The new Voice input (hold fn) action works with input methods that listen while fn is held. - Usage Stats can show a month, a quarter, a year or any range you choose, with a heatmap of the year. - 2.4 GHz receivers from other brands show up under Devices and wait for their mouse or keyboard to be switched on.
**Fixed** - Mose could quit unexpectedly while recognising trackpad gestures. - After changing the language, Add Device and the trackpad page no longer mix two languages.
Requires macOS 15 or later.
